title: Taught to his mother
hookLine: the Theravada story: the Buddha taught the Abhidhamma to his mother in heaven over one rainy season
last: SEVEN BOOKS, ENDING IN THE WEB OF CONDITIONS.

cards: The rains have come, and the Buddha is not on earth. That's how the Theravada story goes. A few days ago on this path, he answered his rivals with the twin miracle at Savatthi, fire and water at once.

Then, tradition says, he rose to a heaven of gods and sat down to teach. In the crowd was the one he had come for: his mother, Maya, who died, tradition says, only days after he was born, and was reborn among the gods.
He never knew her. Now he has a whole rainy season with her.

teach.h: THE WHOLE TEACHING, ONE RAINY SEASON.
teach.b: The story is told in the commentaries, and it's the Theravada answer to a question: where did the Abhidhamma come from? First, what he taught her.
Not a short talk: the whole higher teaching, tradition says, the seven books from yesterday, over one rainy season. Second, how it reached the earth.
Each day, the story goes, the Buddha came down to collect alms food and met his disciple Sariputta, known for his wisdom.

teach.h: EACH DAY, AN OUTLINE TO SARIPUTTA.
teach.b: He gave Sariputta the outline of that day's teaching, the method, not every detail, and Sariputta went back and taught it to the monks in full.
So the tradition says the Abhidhamma comes from the Buddha, through Sariputta, to the monks. Third, why his mother. The commentaries don't make a speech about it, but the shape of the story is plain.
The teaching that takes the mind apart into its smallest pieces was given first as a gift to the woman who gave him a body and then was gone.

teach.h: A SON WHO NEVER GOT TO THANK HER.
teach.b: Some readers hear in it a son who never got to thank her, thanking her with what he had. Fourth, the descent.
At the end of the rains, tradition says, he came back down to the world by a stairway of jewels at a place called Sankassa, with crowds waiting to welcome him.
So the week closes on a gift: a demanding teaching, given as a gift.

how: Theravada Buddhists tell this story of the Abhidhamma's origin, and in some Theravada countries the end of the rains retreat is remembered as the time the Buddha came back down from teaching his mother.

games.q: what does “taught to his mother” mean?
o: the story that the Buddha gave the Abhidhamma to Maya
a lesson on honoring parents from the discourses
the Buddha's first sermon, given to his family at home

games.q: a gift to his mother: tap the pairs.
p: his mother, reborn among the gods

s: in the story, the Buddha taught the Abhidhamma first to the monks
tradition says he taught it first to his mother among the gods, and gave Sariputta the outline each day.
Sariputta taught the monks in full from the outlines
the Buddha gave the method; Sariputta filled it out for the monks.
the story says he came back down by a stairway
tradition says a stairway of jewels, at Sankassa.

games.q: you're the Buddha, teaching your mother among the gods for a whole rainy season. the monks on earth are waiting. what do you do?
o: make them wait until the rains are over
give Sariputta an outline each day to teach them
stop teaching your mother and go back down
games.why: tradition says he came down each day for alms, gave Sariputta the outline, and Sariputta taught the monks in full.

practice: If you'd like, bring to mind your mother, or whoever mothered you: a grandmother, an aunt, a father who did it all, a teacher, a friend, living or gone; if that relationship is hard, choose whoever cared for you, even once, even a little.
Hold them in mind without fixing anything. Then, on each out-breath, give them one thing you've learned, the way the Buddha gave his mother what he knew; a small thing is enough.

wordCard.voice: Taught to his mother. The Theravada story that the Buddha gave the whole Abhidhamma to his mother among the gods, over one rainy season. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: a gift to his mother. The whole higher teaching, given first to her. This week, complete.

sources.ref: Atthasalini, introductory discourse (the Abhidhamma taught in the Tavatimsa heaven; the outline given to Sariputta)
Dhammapada commentary on verse 181 (the twin miracle, the rains in heaven, the descent at Sankassa)
